The '''1988–89 Bundesliga''' was the 26th season of the [[Bundesliga]], the premier football league in [[West Germany]]. It began on 22 July 1988<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=325073|title=Schedule Round 1|publisher=DFB}}</ref> and ended on 17 June 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=325435|title=Archive 1988/1989 Round 34|publisher=DFB}}</ref> [[SV Werder Bremen]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]]. The third-to-last team had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off against the third-placed team from 2. Bundesliga.

==Team changes to 1987–88==
[[FC Homburg]] and [[FC Schalke 04]] were directly relegated to the [[1988–89 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[FC St. Pauli]] and [[Stuttgarter Kickers]]. Relegation/promotion play-off participant [[SV Waldhof Mannheim]] won the [[Penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]] of a decisive third match, which had become necessary after the regular two-legged series ended in an aggregated tie, against [[SV Darmstadt 98]] and thus retained their Bundesliga status.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[Eintracht Frankfurt]] and third-placed [[1988–89 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off. Frankfurt won 3–2 on aggregate and retained their Bundesliga status.
